core_insight: Refactoring is deliberate structural improvement with zero behavior change, made safe by tests and small steps, to lower future change cost and risk.

scenes.voice: Why do teams avoid touching old code even when the business needs change?
scenes.visual: Developer hesitating over a large file, red warning icons on tangled code lines.

scenes.voice: Business needs change. Code accretes. Duplication appears, responsibilities blur. A small change touches five files.
scenes.visual: Layers stacking on a codebase diagram, arrows showing same logic in three places.

scenes.voice: The problem isn't bad code. It's change cost and risk. Velocity drops, defects rise, team avoids the area.
scenes.visual: Graph of change cost climbing steeply with complexity.

scenes.voice: Obvious fix? Rewrite it. But rewrites lose implicit behavior and are high risk. Leave it? Debt compounds.
scenes.visual: Two paths: Rewrite with explosion icon, Leave it with debt pile growing.

scenes.voice: Refactoring is structural improvement with zero behavior change. Tests first as safety net, then one small change, verify, repeat.
scenes.visual: Scaffolding around a house with people inside, small edits highlighted.

scenes.voice: Example: 400 line processPayment. Extract Validate, Charge, Audit, Notify. Introduce FraudProvider interface. Audit becomes queue write. Behavior unchanged, seams created.
scenes.visual: Monolith block splitting into labeled boxes with interface seam.

scenes.voice: Trade-off: capacity now for speed later. No tests means no refactor. Stop when next change is easy, not when code is perfect.
scenes.visual: Flow diagram showing problem to safe steps to preserved behavior.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart TD
Problem[Changing business needs] --> Complexity[Code accretes, coupling rises]
Complexity --> Cost[Change cost and risk increase]
Cost --> Decision{Refactor?}
Decision -->|Yes| SafetyNet[Tests as safety net]
SafetyNet --> SmallSteps[Small safe changes, verify]
SmallSteps --> Preserve[Behavior preserved, structure improved]
Decision -->|No| Debt[Technical debt compounds]

mental_model: Treat code like a house people live in. Refactor by adding scaffolding, moving one load-bearing wall at a time, and verifying nothing collapsed with tests. Improve shape to lower future change cost, not to achieve perfect aesthetics.
final_takeaway: Refactor with tests and small steps to lower change cost and risk, not to make code pretty.
